memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God was with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the desert and became an archer. While he was living in the Desert of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from Egypt. - Gen 21:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the quiet, beautiful conclusion to Ishmael's story: "God was with the boy as he grew up." The child who was sent into the wilderness, who nearly died of thirst, did not merely survive - he thrived, because God was with him. He grew strong, learned to hunt, made a life in the desert. The presence of God turned a place of despair into a place of flourishing.

This is a striking testimony to God's faithfulness. Ishmael was not the child of the covenant promise; the line of Christ would run through Isaac, not him. And yet God was genuinely with Ishmael, caring for him, blessing him, keeping His word to make him into a nation. God's presence and provision reached beyond the central line of His plan.

What made all the difference in Ishmael's life was not his circumstances - the desert was harsh - but God's presence. "God was with the boy." That is the truest security any of us can have. Not comfort, not ease, not favourable circumstances, but the presence of God with us.

This is the promise that runs through all of Scripture and reaches its height in Christ, whose name is Immanuel, "God with us" (Matt 1:23). Jesus promised, "I am with you always, to the very end of the age" (Matt 28:20). Whatever wilderness you find yourself in, the deepest blessing is not escape from the desert but God's presence within it. And that presence is yours in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you find your security in circumstances, or in God's presence?
- How does "God was with the boy" encourage you in your own wilderness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your presence turns even a wilderness into a place of flourishing. Help me find my security not in easy circumstances but in You being with me. Thank You for Immanuel, God with us.
Amen.
